summary: The 59 supplied records overwhelmingly attest I compulsion and its Detransitive necessity counterpart. No new numbered lexical distinction is needed. The explicit Detransitive sense gloss simply labels meanings already represented in the entry.

Human and inanimate coercers occur with active L-series indexing; 87/29 has a postverbal l-marked situation and a bound 1sg patient. Necessity often has no named coercer and takes a bare following finite event, d- plus a finite event, or l- plus Infinitiv. These complement patterns are not separate senses.

Borrowed maǧbur / maǧbūr is invariant across different subjects and can occur with a copula (69/377; JTM 4.4/4), alongside native ǧbiroyo. It is indexed in the existing Nomen Patiens category with its loan status explicit; no Part. Pass. box is invented from an alternative label.

In JTM 1.3/12, broken bread cannot be rejoined. This resembles the entry’s II bone-setting semantic field, but the reduced surface form does not establish the stem. The analysis is withheld pending linguistic confirmation.

Detransitive Infectum-wa in JTM 1.5/27 adds the repeated nighttime work frame. The necessity may be circumstantial rather than a discrete forcing event. No case here establishes an overt ordinary Detransitive agent phrase.

64/221 already belongs to the inherited Preterit references. lu šulṭono may indicate the Sultan’s demand or the beneficiary of the intended marriage request; this single clause does not determine l- as a coercer construction.

The reader’s claimed existing citation at 64/154 is not visible in this input; no entry correction is inferred from that assertion. Existing edition spellings and translation irregularities are retained.

No new numbered sense is warranted. Readers’ D1 is round-1 Detransitive 1. Contrary to repeated reader claims, the Detransitive Infectum-wa box already exists in round-1 proposals; active Infectum-wa at Jan 2.22/3974 is the new box.
Active ǧbərla has an l-indexed feminine causer in Li ʕito ǧbərla i ḥkume. In ǧbərle at Jan 2.18/3719, -le is not an additional patient index. Bound patients are overt in Ġbəralli and ǧbərralli.
Ruḥi in Ǧbərli ruḥi and gədǧəbarno ruḥi is a reflexive patient of the active verb. This differs morphologically from ǧbərno, with the obliged person as Detransitive subject, and creates no idiom.
Bare required events and d-clauses both occur. l sababe mšaḥlfe at Jan 4.I/366 supplies a cause, not evidence for an ordinary expressed human Detransitive agent.

Maǧbur is invariant with hatu and ab babe, the latter accompanied by plural ne. Jan supports round-1 loan-status analysis and Nomen Patiens filing; it does not establish a new native Part. Pass. paradigm.

The Jan collection includes transcribed dialogue and first-person discussion of writing literary Syriac. The reflexive active example at Jan 4.I/168 concerns learning kṯawbonoyo; this is an object of the learning event, not evidence that the entire collection uses a learned verbal paradigm.
